questions.text: Cr2O7^2- ⇌ 2CrO4^2- साम्यावस्था :
questions.text_english: The equilibrium Cr2O7^2- ⇌ 2CrO4^2- :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) exists in basic medium. The dichromate ion (Cr2O7^2-, orange) is the stable form in acidic medium, while the chromate ion (CrO4^2-, yellow) is the stable form in basic medium. When OH- ions are added, the equilibrium shifts forward converting dichromate to chromate; when H+ ions are added, the equilibrium shifts backward. Thus this equilibrium exists in basic medium.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा प्रबलतम अम्ल है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is the strongest acid?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) p-NO2-C6H4COOH. The -NO2 group is a strong electron-withdrawing group. It withdraws electron density from the benzene ring through both inductive and resonance effects, stabilizing the carboxylate anion formed after loss of H+. Greater stabilization of the conjugate base leads to a stronger acid. The -OH group (option B) is electron-donating and weakens the acid, while -Cl (option A) is weakly electron-withdrawing. Plain benzoic acid (option C) has no substituent effect. Hence p-nitrobenzoic acid is the strongest.

questions.text: माल्टोस बना होता है :
questions.text_english: Maltose is made up of :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) glucose and glucose. Maltose is a disaccharide formed by the condensation of two glucose units joined by an alpha-1,4-glycosidic bond. It is obtained by partial hydrolysis of starch. Option A describes sucrose (glucose + fructose), option B describes lactose (glucose + galactose), and option D is incorrect as ribose is a pentose sugar found in nucleotides, not in common disaccharides.

questions.text: अधिकतम क्वथनांकी स्थिरक्वाथी बनाने वाला निकाय है :
questions.text_english: The system that forms maximum boiling azeotrope is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Chloroform and acetone. A maximum boiling azeotrope is formed when the intermolecular interactions between the two components are stronger than those in the pure liquids, causing a negative deviation from Raoult's law. Chloroform and acetone interact strongly through hydrogen bonding (CHCl3 acts as hydrogen bond donor to the carbonyl oxygen of acetone), making their mixture harder to vaporize and giving a higher boiling point than either pure component. CS2 and acetone (option A) form a minimum boiling azeotrope due to positive deviation.

questions.text: शून्य कोटि की अभिक्रिया वह होती है जिसका वेग स्वतंत्र होता है :
questions.text_english: A zero-order reaction is one whose rate is independent of :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Concentration of the reactant. In a zero-order reaction, the rate of reaction is directly proportional to the zeroth power of the concentration of the reactant, i.e., Rate = k[A]^0 = k. This means the rate is constant and does not depend on the concentration of the reactant at all. The rate constant k itself does depend on temperature (Arrhenius equation), but the rate law shows independence from concentration.

questions.text: आर्रेनिअस समीकरण में जब 1/T के साथ log k का ग्राफ खींचा जाता है, तो एक सीधी रेखा प्राप्त होती है जिसकी :
questions.text_english: In the Arrhenius equation, when log k is plotted against 1/T, a straight line is obtained whose :

options.A: ढाल A/R है और अंत:खंड Ea है
options.B: ढाल A है और अंत:खंड -Ea/R है
options.C: ढाल -Ea/RT है और अंत:खंड log A है
options.D: ढाल -Ea/(2.303R) है और अंत:खंड log A है

options_english.A: slope is A/R and intercept is Ea
options_english.B: slope is A and intercept is -Ea/R
options_english.C: slope is -Ea/RT and intercept is log A
options_english.D: slope is -Ea/(2.303R) and intercept is log A

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). The Arrhenius equation is k = A·e^(-Ea/RT). Taking log10 on both sides: log k = log A - Ea/(2.303RT). Rearranging: log k = (-Ea/2.303R)(1/T) + log A. This is of the form y = mx + c, where the slope m = -Ea/(2.303R) and the y-intercept c = log A. Option C is wrong because RT is not a constant; option A and B have incorrect expressions.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रिया के प्रति सर्वाधिक अभिक्रियाशील है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is most reactive towards nucleophilic substitution reaction?
questions.image_description: Option A shows chlorobenzene (benzene ring with a Cl substituent). Option D shows allyl chloride CH2=CH-CH2-Cl.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) CH2=CH-CH2-Cl (allyl chloride). Allyl chloride undergoes nucleophilic substitution very readily because the carbocation intermediate formed after the departure of Cl- is stabilized by resonance with the adjacent double bond (allylic carbocation). Chlorobenzene (option A) is very unreactive due to resonance of lone pair of Cl with the ring and partial double bond character of C-Cl bond. Vinyl chloride (option C) is also very unreactive for the same reason. n-Propyl chloride (option B) undergoes SN2 normally but is not as reactive as allyl chloride.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया में प्राप्त उत्पाद (X) है :
questions.text_english: The product (X) obtained in the following reaction is :

options.A: Cyclohexanone with OH and CHO groups

options_english.A: Cyclohexyl compound with OH and CHO

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). The reagent [Ag(NH3)2]+OH- is Tollens' reagent, which selectively oxidizes aldehyde groups to carboxylate (COO-) without affecting ketone groups. The CHO group in the reactant is oxidized to COO- while the ketone (C=O) on the ring remains unchanged. This gives the product with a cyclohexanone ring bearing a COO- group, which corresponds to option B.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसका क्वथनांक उच्चतम है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following has the highest boiling point?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) CH3COOH (acetic acid). Carboxylic acids have very high boiling points because they exist as hydrogen-bonded dimers through two O-H...O hydrogen bonds, which require considerably more energy to break. CH3COOH also has a higher molecular weight contribution from this dimerization. Aldehydes (CH3CHO) and ketones (CH3COCH3) cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds as donors, though they accept them. CH3COCl is an acid chloride with no hydrogen bonding. Hence acetic acid has the highest boiling point among the four.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किस कारण से फ़ीनॉल नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रिया आसानी से नहीं करता है ?
questions.text_english: Phenol does not undergo nucleophilic substitution reaction easily due to :

options.A: C-OH आबंध में आंशिक द्वि-आबंध लक्षण
options.B: C-C आबंध में आंशिक द्वि-आबंध लक्षण

options_english.A: Partial double bond character of C-OH bond
options_english.B: Partial double bond character of C-C bond

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Partial double bond character of C-OH bond. In phenol, the lone pair of electrons on the oxygen of the -OH group is delocalized into the benzene ring by resonance. This gives the C-O bond a partial double bond character, making it shorter and stronger than a normal C-O single bond. As a result, the C-O bond is difficult to break, so nucleophilic substitution at this carbon does not occur easily. This is unlike aliphatic alcohols where no such resonance exists.

questions.text: CH3-CH(CH3)-CH2-OH के संश्लेषण के लिए मेथेनैल के साथ प्रयुक्त उपयुक्त ग्रीन्यार अभिकर्मक है :
questions.text_english: The suitable Grignard reagent used for the synthesis of CH3-CH(CH3)-CH2-OH with methanal is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) (CH3)2CHMgBr / H2O. The target alcohol is 2-methylpropan-1-ol: (CH3)2CH-CH2-OH. In Grignard synthesis, methanal (HCHO) reacts with RMgBr to give a primary alcohol R-CH2-OH after hydrolysis. So the R group in the Grignard reagent must be (CH3)2CH- (isopropyl group) to give (CH3)2CH-CH2-OH. The Grignard reagent is thus (CH3)2CHMgBr (isopropylmagnesium bromide). Adding this to HCHO followed by hydrolysis gives the desired product.

questions.text: सभी प्रोटीन जल-अपघटन के उपरान्त देते हैं :
questions.text_english: All proteins on hydrolysis give :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) α-amino acids. Proteins are polymers of α-amino acids linked together by peptide bonds (-CO-NH-). When a protein undergoes complete hydrolysis (either by acid, base, or enzymes), the peptide bonds are broken and the constituent α-amino acids are released. Enzymes are themselves proteins, so option A is circular. Glucose is a product of carbohydrate hydrolysis. Polypeptides are intermediate products of incomplete hydrolysis, not the final products.

Reason (R): This is due to greater electron withdrawing nature of F than Cl.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।

options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both the Assertion and Reason are true and Reason correctly explains the Assertion. Fluorine has a higher electronegativity than chlorine, making it a stronger electron-withdrawing group. The stronger inductive (-I) effect of F stabilizes the carboxylate anion (CH2FCOO-) more effectively than Cl does (CH2ClCOO-), making the conjugate base more stable and thus the acid stronger. Therefore, fluoroacetic acid (pKa ≈ 2.6) is indeed a stronger acid than chloroacetic acid (pKa ≈ 2.9).

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). The Assertion is TRUE: p-nitroaniline is indeed a weaker base than p-toluidine because the -NO2 group withdraws electron density from the nitrogen lone pair through resonance, reducing its ability to donate electrons to a proton. However, the Reason is FALSE: the -NO2 group is an electron-withdrawing group (not an electron-donating group as stated in the Reason). It withdraws electron density by resonance (-M effect) and inductive (-I effect), which decreases the basic strength of the amine.

The cyclohexyl radical then reacts with Br2 to give bromocyclohexane (C6H11Br) as the major monohalo product.

sub_questions.solution: Grignard reagents (RMgX) must be prepared under anhydrous conditions because they react readily with water (or any protic solvent) to give an alkane: RMgX + H2O → R-H + Mg(OH)X. Even traces of moisture will decompose the Grignard reagent, making it unavailable for the desired reaction. Anhydrous ether is used as solvent.

sub_questions.text_english: Alkyl halides give alcohol with aqueous KOH whereas in the presence of alcoholic KOH, alkenes are formed. Give reason.

key_points: Aqueous KOH gives OH- which acts as nucleophile (SN2) → alcohol
Alcoholic KOH gives C2H5O- which is bulky base → elimination (E2) → alkene

sub_questions.solution: With aqueous KOH, OH- ions are good nucleophiles and attack the carbon bearing the halogen in an SN2 reaction, substituting Cl- to give an alcohol. With alcoholic KOH (in ethanol), the ethoxide ion (C2H5O-) is a stronger and bulkier base that preferentially abstracts a beta-hydrogen, leading to elimination (E2 mechanism) and forming an alkene instead of substitution.

For a chemical reaction R → P, the variation in the concentration [R] vs time t plot is given as a straight line with negative slope (linear decrease):
(a) Predict the order of the reaction and write the unit of rate constant (k) for this order of reaction.
(b) What is the slope of the curve?

Unit of k is mol L-1 s-1

sub_questions.solution: The graph shows [R] vs t as a straight line with a negative slope, which is characteristic of a zero-order reaction. For a zero-order reaction, [R] = [R]0 - kt, which is a linear equation. The unit of the rate constant k for a zero-order reaction is mol L-1 s-1.

questions.text: आयरन इलेक्ट्रोड का विभव परिकलित कीजिए जिसमें Fe^2+ आयन की सांद्रता 0·01 M है । (298 K पर E°(Fe2+/Fe) = -0·45 V) [दिया गया है : log 10 = 1]
questions.text_english: Calculate the potential of Iron electrode in which the concentration of Fe2+ ion is 0.01 M. (E°(Fe2+/Fe) = -0.45 V at 298 K) [Given: log 10 = 1]

key_points: Apply Nernst equation: E = E° - (0.0591/n) log(1/[Fe2+])
n = 2 for Fe2+/Fe electrode

questions.solution: The electrode reaction is: Fe2+(aq) + 2e- → Fe(s). Using the Nernst equation: E = E° - (0.0591/n) × log(1/[Fe2+]). Here E° = -0.45 V, n = 2, [Fe2+] = 0.01 M. Therefore: E = -0.45 - (0.0591/2) × log(1/0.01) = -0.45 - (0.02955) × log(100) = -0.45 - (0.02955) × 2 = -0.45 - 0.0591 = -0.5091 V. The potential of the iron electrode is approximately -0.509 V.

अभिक्रिया 2NO (g) + Br2 (g) → 2NOBr (g) के लिए निम्नलिखित प्रारंभिक वेग आँकड़े प्राप्त हुए :
[तालिका: प्रयोग 1: [NO]=0.05, [Br2]=0.05, दर=1.0×10-3; प्रयोग 2: [NO]=0.05, [Br2]=0.15, दर=3.0×10-3; प्रयोग 3: [NO]=0.15, [Br2]=0.05, दर=9.0×10-3]
(क) अभिक्रिया में NO और Br2 के प्रति कोटि क्या है ?
(ख) वेग स्थिरांक (k) परिकलित कीजिए ।
(ग) अभिक्रिया वेग निर्धारित कीजिए जब NO और Br2 की सांद्रता क्रमश: 0·4 M और 0·2 M है ।
questions.text_english:
The following initial rate data were obtained for the reaction 2NO(g) + Br2(g) → 2NOBr(g):
[Table: Expt 1: [NO]=0.05, [Br2]=0.05, rate=1.0×10-3; Expt 2: [NO]=0.05, [Br2]=0.15, rate=3.0×10-3; Expt 3: [NO]=0.15, [Br2]=0.05, rate=9.0×10-3]
(a) What is the order with respect to NO and Br2 in the reaction?
(b) Calculate the rate constant (k).
(c) Determine the rate of reaction when concentration of NO and Br2 are 0.4 M and 0.2 M, respectively.

key_points: Order w.r.t. NO = 2, order w.r.t. Br2 = 1, overall order = 3
k = 0.8 L2 mol-2 s-1

questions.solution: Let rate = k[NO]^x[Br2]^y. Comparing experiments 1 and 2 (same [NO], [Br2] changes 3×): 3.0×10-3 / 1.0×10-3 = (0.15/0.05)^y → 3 = 3^y → y = 1. Comparing experiments 1 and 3 (same [Br2], [NO] changes 3×): 9.0×10-3 / 1.0×10-3 = (0.15/0.05)^x → 9 = 3^x → x = 2. So order w.r.t. NO = 2 and w.r.t. Br2 = 1. Using experiment 1: k = rate/([NO]^2[Br2]) = 1.0×10-3 / ((0.05)^2 × 0.05) = 1.0×10-3 / (1.25×10-4) = 8 L2 mol-2 s-1. For [NO]=0.4 M, [Br2]=0.2 M: Rate = 8 × (0.4)^2 × 0.2 = 8 × 0.16 × 0.2 = 0.256 mol L-1 s-1.

questions.text:
जब किसी चालकता सेल को 0·05 M KCl विलयन से भरा जाता है, तो 25ºC पर इसका प्रतिरोध 100 ओम है । जब उसी सेल को 0·02 M AgNO3 विलयन से भरा गया, तो प्रतिरोध 90 ओम था । AgNO3 विलयन की चालकता और मोलर चालकता परिकलित कीजिए ।
(दिया गया है : 0·05 M KCl विलयन की चालकता = 1·35 × 10-2 ohm-1 cm-1)
questions.text_english:
When a certain conductivity cell was filled with 0.05 M KCl solution, it has a resistance of 100 ohm at 25°C. When the same cell was filled with 0.02 M AgNO3 solution, the resistance was 90 ohm. Calculate the conductivity and molar conductivity of AgNO3 solution.
(Given: Conductivity of 0.05 M KCl solution = 1.35 × 10-2 ohm-1 cm-1)

key_points: Cell constant = 1.35 cm-1
Conductivity of AgNO3 = 1.5 × 10-2 ohm-1 cm-1
Molar conductivity = 750 S cm2 mol-1

questions.solution: Step 1 — Find cell constant: Cell constant (G*) = conductivity × resistance = 1.35×10-2 × 100 = 1.35 cm-1. Step 2 — Find conductivity of AgNO3: Conductivity = G*/R = 1.35/90 = 0.015 = 1.5×10-2 ohm-1 cm-1. Step 3 — Find molar conductivity: Molar conductivity (Λm) = (conductivity × 1000)/molarity = (1.5×10-2 × 1000)/0.02 = 15/0.02 = 750 S cm2 mol-1. The conductivity of AgNO3 solution is 1.5 × 10-2 S cm-1 and its molar conductivity is 750 S cm2 mol-1.
questions.topic: Conductance - Cell constant and Molar conductivity

(क) निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा ऐलिलिक हैलाइड है ?
(i) CH3-CH=CH-Br
(ii) CH2=CH-CH(Br)-CH3

(ख) क्लोरोबेन्ज़ीन और 2,4,6-ट्राइनाइट्रोक्लोरोबेन्ज़ीन में से कौन नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन के प्रति अधिक अभिक्रियाशील है और क्यों ?

(ग) C4H9Cl के किस समावयव का न्यूनतम क्वथनांक होता है ?
questions.text_english:
(a) Which of the following is an allylic halide?
(i) CH3-CH=CH-Br
(ii) CH2=CH-CH(Br)-CH3

(b) Out of chlorobenzene and 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene, which is more reactive towards nucleophilic substitution and why?

(c) Which isomer of C4H9Cl has the lowest boiling point?

key_points: (a) (ii) is allylic halide: Br is on carbon adjacent to C=C
(b) 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene is more reactive due to electron-withdrawing NO2 groups
(c) (CH3)3CCl (neopentyl/tert-butyl chloride) has lowest boiling point due to lowest surface area

questions.solution: (a) Option (ii) CH2=CH-CH(Br)-CH3 is an allylic halide because the bromine is attached to a carbon that is adjacent (allylic position) to the carbon-carbon double bond. In option (i), CH3-CH=CH-Br, the Br is directly attached to the sp2 carbon of the double bond, making it a vinylic halide. (b) 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene is far more reactive towards nucleophilic substitution than chlorobenzene. The three strongly electron-withdrawing -NO2 groups at ortho and para positions decrease the electron density on the ring, especially at the carbon bearing Cl, making it highly susceptible to nucleophilic attack. In chlorobenzene, the lone pair of Cl donates electron density to the ring, making it less reactive. (c) Among isomers of C4H9Cl, 2-chloro-2-methylpropane (tert-butyl chloride, (CH3)3CCl) has the lowest boiling point because it has the most branched, nearly spherical shape, resulting in the smallest surface area and weakest van der Waals forces.
questions.topic: Types of halides, Nucleophilic substitution, Boiling points

Potassium tetrahydroxidozincate (II)

[Cr(NH3)5Cl]Cl2, [Cr(NH3)3Cl3], [Cr(NH3)6]Cl3

questions.solution: (a) Potassium tetrahydroxidozincate(II): The central metal is Zn(II), ligand is OH- (hydroxido), coordination number 4 gives [Zn(OH)4]^2-, and with K+ counter ions: K2[Zn(OH)4]. (b) Conductivity is proportional to the number of ions produced in solution. questions.text: यौगिक (A) (C6H12O2), LiAlH4 से अपचयित होकर दो यौगिक (B) और (C) देता है । यौगिक (B) PCC के साथ ऑक्सीकृत होकर यौगिक (D) देता है जो तनु NaOH के साथ अभिकृत करके तदुपरान्त गर्म करने पर यौगिक (E) देता है । यौगिक (E) उत्प्रेरकी हाइड्रोजनन करके पर यौगिक (C) देता है । यौगिक (D) और ऑक्सीकृत होकर यौगिक (F) देता है जो कि एकक्षारकीय अम्ल (अणु भार = 60) पाया गया । यौगिकों (A), (B), (C), (D), (E) और (F) की पहचान कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Compound (A) (C6H12O2) on reduction with LiAlH4 gives two compounds (B) and (C). The compound (B) on oxidation with PCC gives compound (D) which upon treatment with dilute NaOH and subsequent heating gives compound (E). Compound (E) on catalytic hydrogenation gives compound (C). The compound (D) is oxidized further to give compound (F) which is found to be a monobasic acid (Molecular weight = 60). Identify the compounds (A), (B), (C), (D), (E) and (F).

key_points: F is CH3COOH (acetic acid, MW=60, monobasic)
D is CH3CHO (ethanal), since oxidation of D gives acetic acid
B is CH3CH2OH (ethanol), since PCC oxidation of primary alcohol gives aldehyde
E is CH3CH=CHCHO or CH3CH=CH-CHO (but-2-enal/crotonaldehyde from aldol condensation of ethanal)
C is CH3CH2CH2CH2OH? No — E on hydrogenation gives C, C comes from LiAlH4 reduction of ester A

A is ethyl acetate CH3COOC2H5 (C6H12O2 matches with MW=88? No), reconsidering: A=C6H12O2, LiAlH4 gives two alcohols B and C; F=CH3COOH (MW60); D=CH3CHO; B=C2H5OH; E=aldol product crotonaldehyde; C=n-butanol from hydrogenation of crotonaldehyde

A = ethyl propanoate? MW=102 no. A must be an ester that on LiAlH4 reduction gives two different alcohols: ethanol (B, MW=46) and another alcohol C. Since D is ethanal → F is acetic acid, B=ethanol. E= but-2-enal (from aldol of ethanal). C = butan-1-ol (from hydrogenation of but-2-enal). A = butyl acetate? C6H12O2 = MW=116 no. Propyl formate HCOOC3H7 = C4H8O2. Ethyl acetate C4H8O2. A= C6H12O2 could be propyl propanoate C2H5COOC3H7 MW=116 no. Most likely: A=ethyl butyrate or the ester analysis. Correct identification: A = ethyl propanoate (C2H5COOC2H5, MW=102) — does not fit C6H12O2. Reassessing: C6H12O2 MW=116 — propyl propanoate (C3H7COOC3H7? no, that's C7). n-butyl acetate CH3COOC4H9 = C6H12O2 MW=116. LiAlH4 on n-butyl acetate gives ethanol (no, gives butan-1-ol + methanol no). Correct: CH3COOC4H9 → CH3CH2OH? No, ester RCOOC4H9 reduces to RCH2OH + n-C4H9OH. If A=CH3COOC4H9, D from PCC of smaller alcohol would be... This is complex. Final answer: A = ethyl propanoate... Revisiting with F=CH3COOH: D must be CH3CHO. B=C2H5OH. E=CH3CH=CHCHO (crotonaldehyde via aldol). C=CH3CH2CH2CH2OH (n-butanol, from catalytic hydrogenation of crotonaldehyde). A = ester that on LiAlH4 gives C2H5OH (B) and n-C4H9OH (C). This ester is n-butyl acetate: CH3-COO-C4H9 — MW = 116 = C6H12O2. YES. So A=n-butyl acetate (CH3COOC4H9).

questions.solution: Starting from the end: F is a monobasic acid with molecular weight 60, which is acetic acid (CH3COOH). D on further oxidation gives F (CH3COOH), so D is ethanal (CH3CHO) — a primary aldehyde that oxidizes to acetic acid. B on PCC oxidation gives D (CH3CHO), so B is ethanol (CH3CH2OH). D (ethanal) on aldol condensation with dilute NaOH and heating gives E (but-2-enal / crotonaldehyde: CH3CH=CHCHO). E on catalytic hydrogenation gives C, so C is butan-1-ol (CH3CH2CH2CH2OH). Now A (C6H12O2) on LiAlH4 reduction gives B (ethanol) and C (butan-1-ol). This means A is an ester: butan-1-ol + acetic acid form the ester n-butyl acetate: A = CH3COOC4H9 (n-butyl acetate, C6H12O2, MW = 116). Summary: A = n-butyl acetate (CH3COOC4H9), B = ethanol (CH3CH2OH), C = butan-1-ol (C4H9OH), D = ethanal (CH3CHO), E = but-2-enal/crotonaldehyde (CH3CH=CHCHO), F = acetic acid (CH3COOH).

(i) CH3-CH2-CH=CH2 → (a) B2H6 (b) 3H2O2/OH- →

questions.text_english:
(a) Write the mechanism of the following reaction:
CH3CH2OH → (H+/443K) → CH2=CH2

(b) Write the main product in each of the following reactions:
(i) CH3-CH2-CH=CH2 → (a) B2H6 (b) 3H2O2/OH- ->
(ii) Phenol → (a) aq. NaOH (b) CO2, H+ ->

key_points: (a) E1 mechanism: protonation of OH to give oxonium ion, loss of water to give carbocation, loss of H+ from adjacent carbon to give ethene
(b)(i) Anti-Markovnikov addition of water via hydroboration: product is CH3CH2CH2CH2OH (butan-1-ol)
(b)(ii) Kolbe's reaction: phenol + NaOH gives sodium phenoxide; CO2/H+ (carboxylation at 573K) gives salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid)

questions.image_description: Part (b)(ii) shows a phenol structure (benzene ring with OH group) reacting with aqueous NaOH followed by CO2 and H+.
questions.solution: (a) Mechanism of dehydration of ethanol: Step 1 — Protonation: CH3CH2OH + H+ → CH3CH2OH2+ (ethyloxonium ion). Step 2 — Ionization: CH3CH2OH2+ → CH3CH2+ + H2O (carbocation formation). Step 3 — Elimination: CH3CH2+ → CH2=CH2 + H+ (loss of proton from adjacent carbon gives ethene). (b)(i) Hydroboration-oxidation (B2H6 then H2O2/OH-) gives anti-Markovnikov addition of water. The -OH adds to the terminal (less substituted) carbon of but-1-ene. Product: butan-1-ol (CH3CH2CH2CH2OH). (b)(ii) This is Kolbe's reaction. Phenol reacts with aqueous NaOH to form sodium phenoxide (C6H5O-Na+). The sodium phenoxide is then treated with CO2 under pressure and the product is acidified to give salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid, C6H4(OH)COOH).

questions.solution: (a) A peptide linkage (peptide bond) is the amide bond (-CO-NH-) formed by the condensation reaction between the carboxyl group (-COOH) of one amino acid and the amino group (-NH2) of another amino acid, with the elimination of a water molecule. It is the fundamental linkage that joins amino acids in proteins. (b) The two strands of the DNA double helix are held together by hydrogen bonds between the complementary nitrogenous base pairs: adenine (A) forms two hydrogen bonds with thymine (T), and guanine (G) forms three hydrogen bonds with cytosine (C). (c) Starch is a polysaccharide. Sucrose is a disaccharide, glucose and fructose are monosaccharides. (d) Water-soluble vitamin example: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) or Vitamin B complex. Fat-soluble vitamin example: Vitamin A (retinol), Vitamin D, Vitamin E, or Vitamin K.

बैटरियाँ और ईंधन सेल गैल्वेनी सेल के अत्यन्त उपयोगी रूप हैं । विद्युत ऊर्जा के स्रोत के लिए प्रयुक्त कोई भी बैटरी अथवा सेल मूलभूत रूप से गैल्वेनी सेल होता है । तथापि, किसी बैटरी के प्रायोगिक उपयोग के लिए इसे हल्की तथा सुसंबद्ध होना चाहिए एवं प्रयोग में लाते समय इसकी वोल्टता में अधिक परिवर्तन नहीं होना चाहिए । मुख्यत: बैटरियाँ दो प्रकार की होती हैं — प्राथमिक बैटरियाँ और संचायक बैटरियाँ ।

प्राथमिक बैटरियों में, अभिक्रिया केवल एक बार होती है तथा कुछ समय तक प्रयोग के बाद बैटरी निष्क्रिय हो जाती है एवं पुन: प्रयोग में नहीं लाई जा सकती, जबकि संचायक बैटरियाँ पुन:आवेशित की जा सकती हैं ।

ऊष्मीय संयंत्रों से विद्युत उत्पादन बहुत अधिक उपयोगी विधि नहीं है तथा यह प्रदूषण का एक बड़ा स्रोत है । इस समस्या के समाधान के लिए ऐसे गैल्वेनी सेल अभिकल्पित किए गए हैं जिनमें ईंधनों की दहन ऊर्जा को सीधे ही विद्युत ऊर्जा में परिवर्तित किया जाता है, और इन्हें ईंधन सेल कहते हैं । ऐसे ही एक ईंधन सेल को अपोलो अंतरिक्ष कार्यक्रम में प्रयोग में लाया गया था ।
questions.text_english:
Batteries and fuel cells are very useful forms of galvanic cell. Any battery or cell that we use as a source of electrical energy is basically a galvanic cell. However, for a battery to be of practical use it should be reasonably light, compact and its voltage should not vary appreciably during its use. There are mainly two types of batteries — primary batteries and secondary batteries.

In the primary batteries, the reaction occurs only once and after use over a period of time the battery becomes dead and cannot be reused again, whereas the secondary batteries are rechargeable.

Production of electricity by thermal plants is not a very efficient method and is a major source of pollution. To solve this problem, galvanic cells are designed in such a way that energy of combustion of fuels is directly converted into electrical energy, and these are known as fuel cells. One such fuel cell was used in the Apollo space programme.

sub_questions.text: प्राथमिक बैटरियाँ, संचायक बैटरियों से किस प्रकार भिन्न होती हैं ?
sub_questions.text_english: How do primary batteries differ from secondary batteries?

key_points: Primary batteries cannot be recharged; reaction occurs once and battery becomes dead
Secondary batteries are rechargeable by passing electric current

sub_questions.solution: In primary batteries, the electrode reactions occur only once and the battery becomes dead after use; it cannot be recharged or reused. Examples include dry cell and mercury cell. In secondary batteries, the electrode reactions are reversible and the battery can be recharged by passing electrical current through it in the opposite direction. The lead storage battery is a common example of a secondary battery.

sub_questions.text_english: The cell potential of Mercury cell is 1.35 V, and remains constant during its life. Give reason.

key_points: The overall reaction does not involve any ion in solution
Electrolyte (KOH/ZnO paste) concentration does not change during the reaction

sub_questions.solution: The cell potential of the mercury cell remains constant at 1.35 V throughout its life because the overall cell reaction does not involve any ion in aqueous solution whose concentration would change. The electrolyte used is a paste of KOH and ZnO, and since the reaction ZnO + HgO → ZnO + Hg involves solid-phase species, the concentration of the electrolyte (ionic activity) remains unchanged throughout use, keeping the EMF constant.

key_points: Recharging (reverse reactions): At cathode (Pb electrode): PbSO4 + 2H+ + 2e- → Pb + H2SO4
At anode (PbO2 electrode): PbSO4 + 2H2O → PbO2 + H2SO4 + 2H+ + 2e-

questions.text: संयोजकता आबंध सिद्धान्त (VBT) उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों के बनने, चुंबकीय व्यवहार और ज्यामितीय आकृतियों का यथोचित स्पष्टीकरण देता है जबकि 'क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धान्त' उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों में विद्यमान केन्द्रीय धातु परमाणु/आयन के d-कक्षकों की ऊर्जा की समानता पर विभिन्न क्रिस्टल क्षेत्रों के प्रभाव (लिगन्डों को बिंदु आवेश मानते हुए उनके द्वारा प्रदत्त प्रभाव) पर आधारित है । प्रबल तथा दुर्बल क्रिस्टल क्षेत्रों में d-कक्षकों के विपाटन से विभिन्न इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास प्राप्त होते हैं । क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धान्त यह मानता है कि उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों का रंग इलेक्ट्रॉन के d-d संक्रमण के कारण होता है । उपसहसंयोजन यौगिकों की धातुकर्म प्रक्रमों, विश्लेषणात्मक तथा औषध रसायन के क्षेत्र में महत्त्वपूर्ण अनुप्रयोग हैं ।
questions.text_english: The Valence Bond Theory (VBT) explains the formation, magnetic behaviour and geometrical shapes of coordination compounds whereas 'The Crystal Field Theory' for coordination compounds is based on the effect of different crystal fields (provided by ligands taken as point charges), on the degeneracy of d-orbital energies of the central metal atom/ion. The splitting of the d-orbitals provides different electronic arrangements in strong and weak crystal fields. The crystal field theory attributes the colour of the coordination compounds to d-d transition of the electron. Coordination compounds find extensive applications in metallurgical processes, analytical and medicinal chemistry.

sub_questions.text: क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र विपाटन ऊर्जा क्या है ?
sub_questions.text_english: What is crystal field splitting energy?

key_points: Energy difference between the two sets of d-orbitals (eg and t2g) after splitting in an octahedral crystal field, denoted as Δo or 10Dq

sub_questions.solution: Crystal field splitting energy (CFSE) is the energy difference between the higher energy set of d-orbitals (eg: dx2-y2 and dz2) and the lower energy set (t2g: dxy, dyz, dxz) that arises due to the electrostatic influence of surrounding ligands in an octahedral field. It is denoted by Δo (or 10Dq). Electrons occupy the lower t2g orbitals preferentially, and the energy gained is the crystal field stabilization energy.

sub_questions.text: क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धान्त के आधार पर संकुल [Ti(H2O)6]^3+ के बैंगनी रंग का कारण दीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Give reason for the violet colour of the complex [Ti(H2O)6]^3+ on the basis of crystal field theory.

key_points: Ti3+ has one d-electron (d1 configuration)
d-d transition from t2g to eg absorbs yellow-green light, transmitting violet

sub_questions.solution: In [Ti(H2O)6]^3+, titanium is in the +3 state with electronic configuration [Ar]3d1. The single d-electron occupies the lower t2g orbital. When white light falls on this complex, the d-electron absorbs energy corresponding to yellow-green wavelength (~500 nm) and is excited to the higher eg level (d-d transition). Since yellow-green light is absorbed, the complementary colour violet is transmitted, giving the complex its characteristic violet colour.

[Cr(NH3)6]^3+ अनुचुंबकीय है जबकि [Ni(CN)4]^2- प्रतिचुंबकीय है । व्याख्या कीजिए ।
अथवा
[Fe(CN)6]^3- एक आंतरिक कक्षक संकुल है जबकि [Fe(H2O)6]^3+ बाह्य कक्षक संकुल है, व्याख्या कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english:
[Cr(NH3)6]^3+ is paramagnetic while [Ni(CN)4]^2- is diamagnetic. Explain why. [Atomic No.: Cr=24, Ni=28]
OR
Explain why [Fe(CN)6]^3- is an inner orbital complex, whereas [Fe(H2O)6]^3+ is an outer orbital complex. [Atomic No.: Fe=26]

key_points: Cr in [Cr(NH3)6]^3+ is Cr^3+ with d3 configuration; NH3 is weak field ligand; 3 unpaired electrons → paramagnetic
Ni in [Ni(CN)4]^2- is Ni^2+ with d8; CN- is strong field ligand; forces pairing in square planar geometry → all paired → diamagnetic

OR: Fe^3+ is d5; CN- is strong field → pairs electrons in t2g → uses inner 3d orbitals → inner orbital complex; H2O is weak field → electrons remain unpaired in 3d → uses outer 4d orbitals → outer orbital complex

sub_questions.solution: [Cr(NH3)6]^3+: Cr has atomic number 24, so Cr^3+ has configuration [Ar]3d3. NH3 is a weak field ligand that does not cause pairing of electrons. The 3 d-electrons remain in separate d-orbitals (t2g^3) with 3 unpaired electrons. Hence [Cr(NH3)6]^3+ is paramagnetic. [Ni(CN)4]^2-: Ni has atomic number 28, so Ni^2+ has configuration [Ar]3d8. CN- is a very strong field ligand that causes pairing of all electrons. In square planar geometry, the 8 d-electrons pair up completely with no unpaired electrons. Hence [Ni(CN)4]^2- is diamagnetic. OR: Fe (Z=26), Fe^3+ has 3d5 configuration. In [Fe(CN)6]^3-: CN- is a strong field ligand causing pairing of d-electrons into t2g orbitals (t2g^5 eg^0). The inner 3d, 4s, 4p orbitals (d2sp3) are used for hybridization — it is an inner orbital complex with 1 unpaired electron. In [Fe(H2O)6]^3+: H2O is a weak field ligand, electrons remain unpaired (t2g^3 eg^2). The outer 4d orbitals are used (sp3d2 hybridization) — it is an outer orbital complex with 5 unpaired electrons.

Answer any five questions of the following:

sub_questions.text: N,N-डाइएथिल-बेन्ज़ीनसल्फोनैमाइड क्षार में अविलेय होता है — कारण दीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: N,N-diethyl-benzenesulphonamide is insoluble in alkali. Give reason.

key_points: N has no acidic H (both N-H replaced by ethyl groups)
Cannot lose H+ to form water-soluble sodium salt with NaOH

sub_questions.solution: N,N-diethyl-benzenesulphonamide [C6H5SO2N(C2H5)2] is insoluble in alkali because there is no hydrogen atom on the nitrogen — both hydrogens have been replaced by ethyl groups. Secondary sulphonamides (with one N-H) dissolve in alkali by losing the N-H proton to form a water-soluble sodium salt. Since N,N-diethyl compound has no N-H bond, it cannot react with NaOH to form a soluble salt, and hence remains insoluble.

sub_questions.text: ऐनिलीन फ्रीडेल-क्राफ्ट्स अभिक्रिया नहीं करती — क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction. Why?

key_points: Aniline acts as Lewis base and forms a salt with AlCl3 (Lewis acid catalyst)
This deactivates the ring and prevents Friedel-Crafts reaction

sub_questions.solution: Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction because it reacts with the Lewis acid catalyst AlCl3 (used in Friedel-Crafts reaction) to form a salt: C6H5NH2 + AlCl3 → C6H5NH2·AlCl3 (a complex). This protonates or complexes the -NH2 group, converting it to -NH3+ or an AlCl3 complex. The -NH3+ group is strongly electron-withdrawing, which deactivates the benzene ring and prevents electrophilic substitution. Thus Friedel-Crafts reaction cannot occur with aniline.

sub_questions.text: मेथिलऐमीन और ऐनिलीन में विभेद करने के लिए सरल रासायनिक परीक्षण लिखिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Write a simple chemical test to distinguish between methylamine and aniline.

key_points: Azo dye test (coupling reaction): aniline forms diazonium salt → azo dye (orange-red); methylamine does not
Alternatively: carbylamine test or litmus test (methylamine is basic, turns litmus blue; aniline weakly basic)

sub_questions.solution: To distinguish methylamine from aniline, the azo dye test can be used. Treat both amines separately with NaNO2 and dilute HCl at 0-5°C, then add beta-naphthol in NaOH solution. Aniline forms a stable diazonium salt (C6H5N2+Cl-) which couples with beta-naphthol to give an orange-red azo dye. Methylamine being an aliphatic amine does not form a stable diazonium salt at low temperature and no azo dye is formed. The appearance of an orange-red precipitate indicates aniline.

sub_questions.text: गैब्रिएल थैलिमाइड संश्लेषण में सम्मिलित रासायनिक अभिक्रिया लिखिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Write the chemical reaction involved in Gabriel phthalimide synthesis.

key_points: Phthalimide + KOH → potassium phthalimide
Potassium phthalimide + RX → N-alkylphthalimide
N-alkylphthalimide + H2O/H+ or N2H4 → primary amine (RNH2)

sub_questions.solution: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used to prepare primary amines. Step 1: Phthalimide reacts with KOH to form potassium phthalimide (the N-H is acidic): C6H4(CO)2NH + KOH → C6H4(CO)2NK + H2O. Step 2: Potassium phthalimide undergoes nucleophilic substitution with an alkyl halide (RX): C6H4(CO)2NK + RX → C6H4(CO)2NR + KX (N-alkylphthalimide). Step 3: Hydrolysis of N-alkylphthalimide with aqueous acid or hydrazine gives the primary amine: C6H4(CO)2NR + H2O → RNH2 + phthalic acid. This method gives pure primary aliphatic amines free from secondary and tertiary amines.

sub_questions.text: आप ऐनिलीन का p-ब्रोमोऐनिलीन में रूपान्तरण कैसे सम्पन्न करेंगे ?
sub_questions.text_english: How will you convert aniline to p-bromoaniline?

key_points: Step 1: Protect NH2 by acetylation: aniline + CH3COCl → acetanilide
Step 2: Brominate with Br2/CH3COOH to get p-bromoacetanilide (para selectivity)
Step 3: Hydrolyze: p-bromoacetanilide + H2O/H+ → p-bromoaniline + CH3COOH

sub_questions.solution: Direct bromination of aniline gives a tribromo product because the -NH2 group strongly activates the ring. To get p-bromoaniline, the -NH2 group must first be protected. Step 1: Acetylation — treat aniline with acetic anhydride to give acetanilide (C6H5NHCOCH3). This reduces the activating effect of -NH2. Step 2: Bromination — treat acetanilide with Br2 in acetic acid to give predominantly p-bromoacetanilide due to the bulky acetyl group directing bromine to the para position. Step 3: Hydrolysis — heat p-bromoacetanilide with dilute HCl or NaOH to remove the acetyl group and get p-bromoaniline (4-bromoaniline).

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया को पूर्ण कीजिए : बेन्ज़ीन डाइएज़ोनियम क्लोराइड → (i) HBF4, (ii) NaNO2/Cu, Δ
sub_questions.text_english: Complete the following reaction: Benzenediazonium chloride → (i) HBF4, (ii) NaNO2/Cu, heat

key_points: (i) HBF4 converts diazonium chloride to diazonium fluoroborate (stable salt)
(ii) NaNO2/Cu, Δ (Sandmeyer reaction) gives nitrobenzene (C6H5NO2)

sub_questions.solution: The benzenediazonium chloride (C6H5N2+Cl-) reacts with HBF4 to form benzenediazonium tetrafluoroborate (C6H5N2+BF4-), which is a more stable dry diazonium salt. On treatment with NaNO2 and copper powder (Cu) with heating (Sandmeyer-type reaction), the diazonium group (-N2+) is replaced by a nitro group (-NO2), giving nitrobenzene (C6H5NO2) as the final product.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया में A और B की संरचनाएँ लिखिए : बेन्ज़ोइक अम्ल + NH3/Δ → A; A + Br2/NaOH → B
sub_questions.text_english: Write the structures of A and B in the following reaction: Benzoic acid + NH3/heat → A; A + Br2/NaOH → B

key_points: A = benzamide (C6H5CONH2): benzoic acid + NH3 on heating gives amide
B = aniline (C6H5NH2): benzamide + Br2/NaOH undergoes Hoffmann bromamide degradation

sub_questions.solution: Step 1: Benzoic acid (C6H5COOH) reacts with ammonia (NH3) on heating to first form ammonium benzoate, which on further heating loses water to give benzamide. A = C6H5CONH2 (benzamide). Step 2: Benzamide undergoes Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction with Br2 and NaOH (aqueous). The -CONH2 group loses CO2 and the carbon chain shortens by one carbon, giving a primary amine with one fewer carbon. B = C6H5NH2 (aniline). The reaction is: C6H5CONH2 + Br2 + 4NaOH → C6H5NH2 + Na2CO3 + 2NaBr + 2H2O.

(ii) f-ब्लॉक तत्त्वों का सामान्य इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास लिखिए ।

(1) The melting and boiling points of Zn, Cd and Hg are low.
(2) Of the d4 species, Cr2+ is strongly reducing while Mn3+ is strongly oxidizing.
(3) E° value of Cu2+/Cu is +0.34 V.
(ii) Complete and balance the following chemical equations:
(1) KMnO4 → heat
(2) Cr2O7^2- + 6I- + 14H+ →

OR

(b) (i) Out of Cu2Cl2 and CuCl2, which is more stable in aqueous solution and why?
(ii) Write the general electronic configuration of f-block elements.
(iii) Predict which of the following will be coloured in aqueous solution and why? Sc3+, Fe3+, Zn2+ [Atomic number: Sc=21, Fe=26, Zn=30]
(iv) How can you obtain potassium dichromate from sodium chromate?
(v) Why do transition metals and their compounds show catalytic activities?

key_points: (a)(i)(1): Zn, Cd, Hg have fully filled d10 configuration; weak metallic bonding due to non-participation of d-electrons in bonding
(a)(i)(2): Cr2+ (d4) loses one more e- to reach stable d3 half-filled state → strong reducing agent; Mn3+ (d4) gains one e- to reach stable d3 state → strong oxidizing agent
(a)(i)(3): Cu has extra stability of completely filled 3d10 4s1 configuration; 2nd ionization energy is low as 3d electron is removed; hydration energy compensates
(a)(ii)(1): 2KMnO4 → K2MnO4 + MnO2 + O2

questions.solution:
(a)(i)(1) Zn, Cd and Hg have low melting and boiling points because they have completely filled d-orbitals (d10 configuration). The d-electrons do not participate in metallic bonding, so only weak metallic bonds (involving s-electrons) are present. This results in low melting and boiling points compared to other transition metals. (a)(i)(2) Both Cr2+ and Mn3+ are d4 species. Cr2+ is a strong reducing agent because it readily loses one electron to achieve the more stable d3 configuration (half-filled t2g). Mn3+ is a strong oxidizing agent because it readily gains one electron to achieve the stable d4 → actually d4 to d5 (half-filled): Mn3+ (d4) gains an electron to become Mn2+ (d5, half-filled), which is more stable. (a)(i)(3) The E° value of Cu2+/Cu is positive (+0.34 V) because copper has an anomalous electronic configuration [Ar]3d10 4s1. The high hydration energy of Cu2+ ion and the extra stability of the completely filled 3d10 configuration of Cu make it favorable for Cu to lose electrons, giving a positive E° value. (a)(ii)(1) 2KMnO4 → K2MnO4 + MnO2 + O2. (a)(ii)(2) Cr2O7^2- + 6I- + 14H+ → 2Cr3+ + 3I2 + 7H2O.

OR (b)(i) CuCl2 is more stable in aqueous solution. Cu+ (in Cu2Cl2) has a tendency to disproportionate in water: 2Cu+(aq) → Cu(s) + Cu2+(aq), because Cu+ has a higher reduction potential. The disproportionation is thermodynamically favorable. Cu2+ (in CuCl2) does not disproportionate. (b)(ii) General electronic configuration of f-block elements: (n-2)f^1-14 (n-1)d^0-1 ns^2. (b)(iii) Fe3+ will be coloured in aqueous solution. Fe (Z=26), Fe3+ has configuration [Ar]3d5 — it has unpaired d-electrons allowing d-d transitions, giving colour. Sc3+ (Z=21) has configuration [Ar] — no d-electrons, colourless. Zn2+ (Z=30) has configuration [Ar]3d10 — completely filled d-orbitals, no d-d transitions possible, colourless. (b)(iv) Sodium chromate (Na2CrO4) is treated with dilute H2SO4 to convert chromate to dichromate in acidic solution: 2Na2CrO4 + H2SO4 → Na2Cr2O7 + Na2SO4 + H2O. Then potassium chloride (KCl) is added to precipitate potassium dichromate: Na2Cr2O7 + 2KCl → K2Cr2O7 + 2NaCl. (b)(v) Transition metals and their compounds act as catalysts because they can exhibit variable oxidation states, allowing them to form unstable intermediate compounds with reactants, providing an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy. They can also provide a surface for adsorption of reactant molecules (heterogeneous catalysis), thereby increasing the effective concentration and facilitating bond breaking.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) At the same temperature, CO2 gas is more soluble in water than O2 gas. Which one of them will have higher value of KH and why?
(ii) How does the size of blood cells change when placed in an aqueous solution containing more than 0.9% (mass/volume) sodium chloride?
(iii) 1 molal aqueous solution of an electrolyte A2B3 is 60% ionized. Calculate the boiling point of the solution. (Given: Kb for H2O = 0.52 K kg mol-1)

OR

(b) (i) The vapour pressures of A and B at 25°C are 75 mm Hg and 25 mm Hg, respectively. If A and B are mixed such that the mole fraction of A in the mixture is 0.4, then calculate the mole fraction of B in vapour phase.
(ii) Define colligative property. Which colligative property is preferred for the molar mass determination of macromolecules?
(iii) Why are equimolar solutions of sodium chloride and glucose not isotonic?

key_points: (a)(i): O2 will have higher KH (Henry's law constant); higher KH means lower solubility; CO2 is more soluble so it has lower KH
(a)(ii): Blood cells shrink (crenation) when placed in hypertonic solution (>0.9% NaCl); water moves out by osmosis
(b)(ii): Colligative property depends on number of solute particles; osmotic pressure preferred for macromolecules
(b)(iii): NaCl dissociates into 2 ions (Na+ + Cl-) while glucose does not dissociate; equimolar NaCl has twice as many particles as glucose → higher osmotic pressure → not isotonic

questions.solution:
(a)(i) O2 will have a higher value of KH. According to Henry's law, the solubility of a gas is inversely proportional to KH (higher KH = lower solubility). Since CO2 is more soluble in water than O2 at the same temperature, CO2 has a lower KH value, and O2 has a higher KH value. CO2 also reacts with water to form carbonic acid, which additionally contributes to its higher solubility. (a)(ii) When blood cells are placed in a solution more concentrated (hypertonic) than 0.9% NaCl, the surrounding solution has a higher osmotic pressure. Water molecules move out of the blood cells by osmosis (from lower concentration inside to higher concentration outside). As a result, the blood cells shrink — a process called crenation (plasmolysis). (a)(iii) A2B3 → 2A3+ + 3B2- (5 ions per formula unit). Van't Hoff factor: i = 1 + (n-1)×α = 1 + (5-1)×0.60 = 1 + 2.40 = 3.40. Elevation in boiling point: ΔTb = i × Kb × m = 3.40 × 0.52 × 1 = 1.768 K. Boiling point of solution = 100 + 1.768 = 101.768°C ≈ 101.77°C.

OR (b)(i) Mole fraction of A in liquid = 0.4, so mole fraction of B in liquid = 0.6. PA = xA × PA° = 0.4 × 75 = 30 mm Hg. PB = xB × PB° = 0.6 × 25 = 15 mm Hg. Ptotal = 30 + 15 = 45 mm Hg. Mole fraction of B in vapour phase: yB = PB/Ptotal = 15/45 = 1/3 ≈ 0.333. (b)(ii) A colligative property is a property of a solution that depends only on the number of solute particles (molecules or ions) present per unit volume of solvent, regardless of the nature of the solute. The four colligative properties are relative lowering of vapour pressure, elevation in boiling point, depression in freezing point, and osmotic pressure. Osmotic pressure is preferred for determining the molar mass of macromolecules because it gives a measurable value even at very low concentrations, and tiny differences in osmotic pressure can be measured with precision. (b)(iii) Equimolar solutions of NaCl and glucose are not isotonic because NaCl is a strong electrolyte that completely dissociates into two ions (Na+ and Cl-) per formula unit, giving twice as many particles as glucose (which is a non-electrolyte and does not dissociate). As a result, the equimolar NaCl solution has twice the osmotic pressure of the glucose solution, making them non-isotonic.
